questions.prompt: What is the shape of the DNA molecule?
options: A twisted double-stranded ladder called a double helix
questions.explanation: DNA is made of two strands wound around each other, forming the familiar twisted ladder shape called a double helix.
questions.misconception: Some draw DNA as a straight line or a tangled mess, but the regular double-helix twist is exactly what allows it to copy itself faithfully.

questions.prompt: Which bases pair together in DNA?
options: A pairs with T, and G pairs with C
A pairs with G, and T pairs with C
A pairs with A, and T pairs with T
questions.explanation: The four bases pair in a fixed pattern: A (adenine) with T (thymine), and G (guanine) with C (cytosine).
questions.misconception: Learners sometimes mix up the pairing letters. The fixed rule (A-T, G-C) is what lets one strand make an exact copy of the other.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of DNA?
options: To store the instructions that build and run an organism
To generate energy for the cell
questions.explanation: DNA holds the genetic code - the instructions living things use to build themselves and stay alive.
questions.misconception: Energy production is actually the job of the mitochondrion, not DNA. DNA carries information, not power.

questions.prompt: Where is most of a cell's DNA found?
options: On the outside of the cell
questions.explanation: Most DNA is packed into the nucleus, where it is protected and kept as the master instruction set. A little extra DNA lives in the mitochondria.
questions.misconception: DNA is not spread across the outside or wall of the cell - it is stored in the nucleus as the master instruction set (with a little extra in mitochondria).

questions.prompt: How is RNA different from DNA?
options: RNA is usually single-stranded and can leave the nucleus
RNA is double-stranded and stays in the nucleus
questions.explanation: RNA is usually single-stranded and smaller. It copies the instructions from the nucleus and carries them out to where proteins are made. DNA is double-stranded and stays put.
questions.misconception: RNA is not just DNA by another name. Being single-stranded and able to travel out of the nucleus is what makes RNA a real, separate molecule.
